name: John Kapantzakis
title: Senior Software Engineer
summary: Senior Software Engineer with 12+ years building data-intensive web products across React, Next.js, Node.js, and Ruby on Rails. Currently developing AI-assisted observability features and frontend performance improvements at Netdata Cloud, with prior work shipping merchant, search, and e-commerce products.

experience.context: Open-source, real-time observability platform. Frontend of Netdata Cloud, a large, data-intensive React application.
bullets: Developed AI assistant frontend capabilities for Netdata Cloud, including persistent LLM conversations, Netdata-specific tools, and investigation workflows, plus Model Context Protocol (MCP) frontend support.
Improved React performance by reducing unnecessary remounts and data-processing overhead.
Reduced frontend CI runtime by about 60% through Jest test sharding and test-reliability fixes.

Built and evolved the Dynamic Configurations UI for dynamically generated forms, and contributed to AI Insights reports plus enterprise identity features including SCIM, SSO, role and room mappings, and label-driven room membership.

experience.context: Job search engine used by 15M+ jobseekers a month across 20 countries.
bullets: Built Labour Market Intelligence, a new data product, from zero to launch in under a year on Next.js, working in a team of three.
Implemented interactive charts and maps with Apache ECharts, search, grouping, and filtering so users could explore hiring demand, salaries, and trends across multiple countries.

experience.context: One of Greece's leading e-commerce marketplaces. Partners department: tooling for merchants.
bullets: Developed and maintained the merchant platform for orders, payments, and daily operations using Ruby on Rails, Hotwire Turbo, and React.

Contributed two features to Hotwire Turbo that shipped in Turbo 7 and were credited in the release announcement, and published two engineering articles on progressive data loading in React and lazy loading with Hotwire.

experience.context: Greek business-software company. Epsilon ESS, an employee self-service web platform on ASP.NET and C#.
bullets: Progressed from junior web designer to full-stack developer responsible for the product frontend, implementing features end to end across C# backend and TypeScript frontend.

Introduced TypeScript, webpack, Redux-managed asynchronous views, and unit tests with Mocha, Chai, and xUnit, then built a Node.js and Handlebars CLI to generate form boilerplate across UI, state, and data models.

projects.name: hoohooli.gr
projects.context: Family business: a live Greek e-shop for handmade baby and toddler clothes. A WordPress/WooCommerce monolith split into a Next.js storefront and a headless WooCommerce backend.
bullets: Moved the product catalogue to a Next.js 16 App Router storefront on Vercel. Kept checkout, payments and accounts on WordPress behind an API subdomain, restyled to match the new UI.
Carried the cart across both apps through a server-side proxy to the CoCart API, with a cart-key handoff to WooCommerce checkout.
Cut product API payloads from ~2.4 MB to ~400 KB so they fit the Next.js data cache. Added indexable category routes, a live sitemap and Product/Breadcrumb structured data.
